Surya's rows move here from docs next, under the keeper lease (docs decision 2026-11-17-commons-and-device-bases).
considered: Recording this in docs as before; the base is the place from now on, so its first row is its own making.

title: The cameras' fault, understood
done: Both cameras stay broken, but for a stated reason and with a way in: nothing describes the sensors; the wiring of seven slots is known from the vendor's kernel; the models are not.
considered: Naming sensor models from reports.
rejected: That: hearsay until a chip answers.

title: The microphone's chain, nearly whole
done: For the first time the test kernel brought the whole microphone chain up to the codec; one timeout stands between it and a sound card. Measured: the right channel is the bottom speaker.
considered: Booting again without reading the bootloader's record.
rejected: That: three wrong theories cost three reboots.

title: The microphone: the route is set, the stream does not start
done: In the test kernel the main-microphone route sets cleanly; starting a recording fails as the TX SoundWire bus loses the codec when it is reshaped for the stream. Power management ruled out. Next: the bus and port parameters, against the phone's Android kernel.
considered: Keeping the bus awake.
rejected: That as the answer.

title: Deep sleep researched: the path chosen and measured where it starts
done: The first feature research (prompts/feature-research.md), signed research-deep-sleep. surya read without a change: s2idle only, OS-initiated PSCI, the SoC's sleep counters readable, no suspend yet in a measured boot, CX collapse and AOSS sleep at 0, the audio DSP never asleep, the deepest cluster state never entered. Six research rows (how Qualcomm reaches its floor, what blocks it, the SM7150 cluster parameters against surya's own tables, waking for calls, the other ways, surya measured), the decision with four ways rejected, six steps on the backlog each with its proof, a deep-sleep part with surya's row unknown, and the check soc-sleeps in lab-tools' suite. docs now shares its research and sources tables.

title: Flashed by devlab; the shell flash script retired
done: surya flashed from the pristine stock image by devlab flash and brought back by devlab provision, all 20 checks passing; flash.sh removed, as planned once devlab had done a real flash. A new check, root-fills-its-partition: the first boot had left the system at 2 GB on a 104 GB partition.
considered: Keeping flash.sh as a fallback.
rejected: That: two ways to flash drift apart; the shell original stays in git history.

title: Both speakers heard - then withdrawn
done: With the author's EarPods as the lab's microphone, devlab hear played a 1000 Hz tone on each speaker and heard both: left at -24.0 dBFS, right at -29.2 dBFS, each over 70 dB above the silent room. The tones are in the manifest. Observed, not judged: the right read 5 dB quieter - the microphone's place or the speakers themselves; one measurement cannot say. WITHDRAWN the same day: the microphone was worn by the author and moved; neither the levels nor the 5 dB difference can be relied on.
considered: Calling the 5 dB a fault.
rejected: That, on one measurement from one position.

title: The lab's idea, told for anyone
done: What this lab is - one particular phone, everything true of it written down, experiments that fall back by themselves - as a piece of writing for a reader who knows nothing of it.
rejected: A list of files.

title: The suspend crash found: a FastRPC helper attached at suspend
done: After the flash the audio DSP died on every suspend attempt (the attempts abort at once: the USB link cannot go idle). Found by experiment, one change at a time: not a first-boot effect (9 of 9 on the second boot), not the sensor proxy (15 of 15 without it), but hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper - 0 of 8 without it, and 0 of 9 on a clean boot with it masked, all 21 checks passing. Masked in the manifest, so every flash has it. The check's resume counter, which always said 0, rewritten in awk and checked against a boot with 24.
considered: A hand-made change the manifest lacked; a first-boot effect; the sensor proxy; a stream left open.
rejected: All four, each by its own measurement. The old 'rare' crash was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down.

title: What the ear heard is withdrawn
done: The microphone was the author's earphones, worn on his head: its distance from the phone changed as he moved. The levels measured, the difference seen between the two speakers, and the passes themselves cannot be relied on. The heard checks are out of the baseline and the lab's microphone is un-named until one is fixed in place; the tool stays, proven to work mechanically.
considered: Keeping the results with a caveat.
rejected: That: evidence from an instrument that moves is not evidence, and a later failure would have looked like the phone getting worse.

title: The USB link no longer flaps
done: Reported by the author: the phone kept reconnecting on his PC (26 USB disconnects in 5 minutes on the lab machine). On USB a suspend cannot complete, and the shell retried every 12 seconds, each attempt dropping the link. A small service holds a kernel wake lock while the port is connected to a host - independent of any shell - baked in by the manifest, with a check. Known before, never written down: it is now.
considered: Changing the shell's suspend hook.
rejected: That: a fix inside one shell does not hold under another, or under none.

title: More of the phone, measured
done: Eight of the phone's twenty parts stood as unknown. The checks now also ask: is Wi-Fi joined and does the gateway answer; is Bluetooth powered and does it hear anything; is there a SIM and is the modem ready; does the kernel expose a headset-jack detector, a fingerprint reader, any motion or light sensor, any image sensor behind the camera pipeline. All read-only.
considered: Marking parts as working from a device node alone.
rejected: That: there and set up is what a machine can prove; the rest are witnessed tests.

title: The port table cleared; a boot spent on a missing tool
done: The TX bus's port layout and timings match mainline sm8250 and the vendor's layout for the ports in use - not the cause. A boot to dump the SoundWire registers found this kernel has no SoundWire debugfs.
considered: Seven ports against the vendor's five as the cause.
rejected: That, after comparing the ports actually used. And booting before checking the tool exists - a lesson: check the instrument first.

title: Why the cameras are dark, and the way in
done: Read from the phone and from sources, changing nothing: the camera pipeline and its control buses work; the phone's description lists no sensor. The vendor's kernel yields the wiring of seven sensor slots but no model names. Written up with the wiring table and a four-step way in (research/cameras.md).
considered: Describing the sensors from the models reported for this phone elsewhere.
rejected: That: hearsay. A chip should say what it is, on its own bus, before a driver is bound to it.

title: The microphone codec comes up
done: Traced the codec's timeout to a bus clash on the microphone-side SoundWire bus, and that to one pin muxed to the wrong function in the audio pin driver (and one more on the receive side), read against the phone's own Android kernel. Corrected and rebuilt: the codec initialises and the sound card is made with it. Recording through it is next.
considered: The macros' autosuspend; the upstream revert (it gives no reason).
rejected: Guessing at clock fixes.

title: The microphone's chain, nearly whole
done: Booted the microphone test kernel (after finding the earlier tries had been given a gzip kernel): for the first time everything up to the codec came up; the card fails on one timeout. Measured which speaker is the bottom one. Saw a boot with no sound card and recorded it.
considered: Theories about the bootloader.
rejected: Acting before reading the bootloader's own record.

title: The modem with a SIM
done: The SIM is seen and ready (1&1). The modem stays shutting-down and refuses to go online, even after a reboot; it loops on one file through tqftpserv, ending each read itself. One theory - a missing read-write directory - was checked and is wrong: the directory exists.
considered: A missing directory.
rejected: That: the program's own paths showed it exists.

title: The map to a first recording
done: Listed the codec's recording side in the test kernel and read how the phone's own Android build routes its main microphone; the names match closely. Found that the kernel branch's pin driver differs from the tested tree - the fix is to be ported, not pasted.
considered: Pasting the table change into the branch.
rejected: That: the branch's driver is not the one that was tested.

title: Two recording tries
done: The main-microphone route from the phone's Android build sets cleanly in the test kernel; the capture stream fails when it starts - the TX bus loses the codec exactly when it is reshaped for the stream. Ruled out power management. Measured the audio processor's once-a-second handover signal.
considered: Keeping the bus awake.
rejected: That as the answer: it changed nothing.

title: surya checks its own health after every boot
done: The manifest says what surya is expected to have ([health]: its sound card, three signal processors and what rests on each, the known boot warnings and failed unit with their reasons, and four known gaps - fingerprint, sensors, both cameras); its amplifier checks moved to tests/health/base. devlab suite put the suite on the phone; after a reboot it ran by itself and said healthy: 29 pass, 4 in known gaps, 1 not measured (no SIM card seen: the modem reports sim-missing).

title: Telegram at provisioning: telegram-desktop, held by Alpine v3.24
done: The author asked for a Telegram client at provisioning as firefox is. Alpine ships one Telegram client for aarch64, the official telegram-desktop (no tdlib, no libpurple Telegram plugin for chatty, no Kotatogram); it went into provision/packages.txt (surya-lab #108). Installing it on the phone failed: v3.24 community ships 6.8.5-r0 linked to libada.so.3 while ada is now 4.0, so apk cannot resolve it even after apk update. devlab provision installs the list in one apk add, so the line would have failed firefox and i2c-tools too; it now waits there as a comment (surya-lab fix right after #108). Edge has 7.4.4-r0 rebuilt against libada.so.4. Nothing was installed or changed on the phone.
considered: Installing telegram-desktop from the edge repository for one package: it would pull edge libraries into a v3.24 system that another session is testing audio on.
rejected: chatty with a Telegram plugin: no such plugin is packaged. Keeping the line live: it breaks the whole package list.

title: How the phone stands
done: Hand-over from the bring-up session (2026-11-17, ~10:00 UTC) to the phone keeper. RUNS: kernel 7.1.0-sm7150-calls+ is the KEPT default (boot entry pmos-calls.conf, blessed); built from linux-phone-oco/linux branch test/surya-calls = tas2562 fixes + PR3 (LPI SoundWire pin mux) + PR5 (SoundWire controllers at 0x62ed/0x62ef, no DCODEC vote) + PR4 (WCD9375 reset: active-low, gpio mux, no sleep state) + PR6 (capture through swr2 DAI 1) + PR7 (q6voice from pulpoff/linux-surya). The proven microphone-only kernel (pmos-mic, 7.1.0-sm7150-mic+) is still installed as a fallback; stock (7.1.0-rc3-sm7150) boots after 3 bad boots. The old /lib/modules/7.1.0-rc3-sm7150-wcd belongs to a removed experiment and can go. HEALTHY: the last runs say healthy, 37-39 pass, 4 known gaps (fingerprint, sensors, both cameras). WORKS, proven by the phone itself: speakers (stereo), earpiece (= the top TAS2564 speaker; the WCD9375 EAR amplifier is silent), both microphones (bottom ADC1, top ADC2 at INP3) through the UCM profile, mobile data (Vodafone.de LTE; tqftpserv 1.3 from Alpine edge, a gsm connection with no APN), SMS (texts its own number, telephony layer, daily), calls both ways (q6voice, Voice Call UCM verb, q6voiced on PCM 0,6, devlab-call-uplink, daily call-echo to blueSIP's echo line +49 89 721010 99701 - its announcement lasts ~19 s). MUST NOT BE UNDONE: the VoiceMMode1 TX Topology 69488 set in the HiFi verb at boot (the DSP builds its voice processor once, at the first call of a boot; a call set up with the default 0x10F71 keeps the uplink silent until a reboot); the codec node has no sleep pin state (ASoC holds it in reset otherwise); /etc/modprobe.d/devlab-pd-mapper.conf (loads qcom_pd_mapper before the ADSP; without it ~1 boot in 5 has no sound card); tqftpserv@edge (1.1.1 keeps the modem in shutting-down); the SIM's own number lives only in ~/.config/devlab/xiaomi-surya/own-number and /etc/devlab/private/own-number - never in a repository. Test sounds are -6 dBFS at 20% (the author: soft). The SIM is in slot 2 (slot 1: no ATR). Never read /sys/kernel/debug/gpio or the LPI pinctrl at 62b40000 (manifest hazards).
considered: next: (1) headphones and the headset mic: need a headset plugged in and the author listening (verify-headphone-mic-earpiece; the jack detector exists since the WCD fixes). (2) upstream, waiting for the author to send: upstream-queue linux/sm7150-wcd 0001-0004 (sm7150-mainline), the tas2562 pair, upstream-alpine-tqftpserv, upstream-pd-mapper-order; q6voice is out of tree (sdm845-mainline) - its upstreaming is not ours yet. (3) the kernel is not yet a package: the kept kernel lives only on the phone's boot partition; a reflash returns stock until it goes through the package conveyor (device.toml carries the userspace side: UCM, q6voiced conf, call-uplink, pd-mapper, tqftpserv@edge, the mobile connection). (4) the deep-sleep steps, sensors, off-state charging, as the queue orders.

title: Deep sleep's way back: decided before the next suspend
done: Looked around (research 2026-11-17-surya-way-back-inventory): the stock qcom_wdt is stopped in late suspend, so it would not have rescued the first hang; ramoops (4 MiB) and a settable RTC exist. Decided (2026-11-17-deep-sleep-way-back): a patched qcom_wdt module that stays armed through sleep, the RTC set, the log from ramoops; built it for the running kernel (vermagic matches), wrote sleep/way-back.sh and sleep/build-wdt.sh.
considered: Timed reboot, USB awake, pstore alone, a kernel rebuild, serial console.
rejected: See the decision.

title: The way back proven; the Bluetooth-blocked hang reproduced and recovered
done: Built and installed the patched qcom_wdt (updates/, stock behaviour until enabled); sleep/way-back.sh verbs check/install/enable/fuse/defuse/collect/cycle. Idle fuse, a probe through a real s2idle entry and the one measured cycle (BT blocked, 15 s) all ended with the watchdog resetting the phone and the phone booting by itself; the cycle hung at suspend entry as before. pstore is empty after a bite; the journal keeps the marker.
considered: A longer fuse (the watchdog counts 32 s at most), setting the RTC (not settable).
rejected: ramoops as the log (does not survive the reset).

Put the script on the phone with devlab phone put and run it with systemd-run (never nohup). After any try that ends in a bite: one clean reboot, read the health. Must not be undone: sensorspd and rootpd stay masked.

title: sleep-wake-uart: the wake found (irq 158) and turned off; a cycle of 15 s that lasts, the SoC still not asleep
done: Looked first: mainline serial_core/qcom_geni_serial/hci_qca read (research 2026-11-17-qca-uart-wake-across-suspend). Traced one short cycle with Bluetooth up: the wake is irq 158 (GPIO 41, the UART RX wake pin, '88c000.serial:wakeup'), not 157. Added way-back.sh cycle SLEEP bt-on (serial power/wakeup off for the cycle, restored after; qcom_stats before/after, RTC-measured sleep, hci0 check). Tests: cycle 5 bt-on twice and cycle 15 bt-on once, all three woke by the RTC alarm (RTC 7, 7, 17 s), the watchdog defused each time, hci0 scanning after, no bite, no reboot needed. Counters from the SoC after the 15 s cycle: cxsd 0, aosd 0, ddr 0, adsp 0 (as before); soc-sleeps fails: 'suspended, yet the SoC never reached its lowest state: cxsd 0, aosd 0; suspends this boot: 7; processors never asleep: adsp; wake locks: devlab-usb'. Whether the cluster low-power states were entered in these cycles: not known yet (cpuidle residency not read in way-back).
considered: Rejected for the wake: rfkill block, unbinding hci_uart/btqca, a device-tree change, a udev rule now (decision 2026-11-17-serial-wakeup-off).
